contexts.text: To this kind of hunting, nets are wont to be attributed.
The reticular work of the altar.
To spread a net over him () = to entice by the delights of earthly loves, and by reasonings from them.
As a snare, a gin, and a net = such things, they also = the destruction of spiritual life, and thus perdition...
Thou shalt make for it a grating the work of a net () = the Sensuous, which is the ultimate. Explained.

(So) everywhere in the outermosts of the body there are reticular forms, and as it were sieves or gratings, by which the things which approach from the world are sifted... There are such most exquisite forms in the stomach... The case is the same with the Sensuous...
The net () = the outermost of life, which corresponds to the interior life, which is of the understanding and will.
The net shall be even to the middle of the altar () = the extension of the Sensuous; the net = the Sensuous.
They were girded with fishing nets as it were, around the loins, through which their nakednesses appeared.
He could thus cast him into his own net.
They said that they would wrap them in a net, and cast them into the sea.
All whom he thus collected he wrapped in a great net, for by phantasies he induced a great net...
Under Spider, see this reference.
Those who are being cast down from those places, appear as it were to be drawn in a net...
What is meant by dragging a net...
The works of those who (teach others, and reform by means of knowledges) are meant by the letting out and the spreading out of nets. Illustrated.
To gather into his net () = into what is evil and false.
From these things it may now be evident what is meant by the nets, etc. which are so often mentioned in the New Testament. Illustrated.

There are good natural men and evil natural men, and the separation of these appears in the Spiritual World like a net let out into the sea, drawing together the fish, and hauling them up on the shore.

Let down the net on the right side of the ship () = that they should teach the good of life. That thus they would convert the gentiles to the Church is signified by their finding abundance, so that they were not able to draw the net on account of the multitude of fishes. AE 513:12.
Under Fish, see this reference.
